components.note: 钅 (metal) — locks are made of metal
The right part (⺌ over 贝) is what remains of the old phonetic that gave the sound suǒ

example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ mén suǒ hǎo.
example.english: Please lock the door.
example.fact: 锁 is both the noun (一把锁, with the measure word 把) and the verb (锁门, 锁上). It is handy in modern vocabulary too: 锁屏 means to lock a phone screen, and 封锁 means to blockade.

meanings: measure word for sets and pairs

components.note: 刂 (knife) — the original idea was splitting something into two parts
畐 (fú) gives the sound — a near match for fù

example.hanzi: 他是我们公司的副经理。
example.pinyin: Tā shì wǒmen gōngsī de fù jīnglǐ.
example.english: He is the deputy manager of our company.
example.fact: 副 as a prefix means "deputy" or "vice": 副总统, 副校长, 副经理. As a measure word it counts matching sets: 一副眼镜 (a pair of glasses), 一副手套 (a pair of gloves), 一副扑克 (a deck of cards). 副作用 is a side effect.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — a kiss is done with the mouth
勿 (wù) gives a loose sound hint for wěn

example.pinyin: Tā qīngqīng de wěn le tā.
example.english: He gently kissed her.
example.fact: 吻 is the romantic or literary "kiss", used as both verb and noun (一个吻). In everyday speech people say 亲 (qīn) instead: 亲一下. 吻合 is an unrelated figurative use meaning "to match".

components.note: 罒 (net) — a net that catches wrongdoers
非 (wrong, not) — doing what is wrong

example.pinyin: Tā fàn le hěn dà de zuì.
example.english: He committed a serious crime.
example.fact: 罪 is a crime or sin, as in 犯罪 (commit a crime) and 罪犯 (criminal). A colloquial twist is 受罪 ("endure guilt"): it means to suffer or go through hardship, as in 这天气真受罪, "this weather is torture".

components.note: 辶 (walk) — fleeing is a movement away
兆 (zhào) gives only a loose sound hint for táo

example.pinyin: Xiǎotōu cóng chuānghu táozǒu le.
example.english: The thief escaped through the window.
example.fact: 逃 is to flee, often with a direction complement: 逃走, 逃跑. It also covers evading obligations, as in 逃课 (skip class) and 逃避 (avoid facing something, such as 逃避责任).

components.note: A picture of a knife with a curved blade and a back edge

example.pinyin: Zhè bǎ dāo hěn fēnglì.
example.english: This knife is very sharp.
example.fact: 刀 counts with 把 (一把刀). It forms 菜刀 (kitchen knife), 刀子 (knife) and 刀工 (knife skills in cooking). As the radical 刂 on the right of characters it signals cutting, as in 别 and 划.

components.note: 心 (heart) — a wish or willingness is a matter of the heart
原 (yuán) gives the sound — a near match for yuàn

example.pinyin: Wǒ yuànyì bāng nǐ.
example.english: I'm willing to help you.
example.fact: 愿 appears mostly in 愿意 (be willing), which is about consent or willingness rather than just wanting (想). It also forms 愿望 (wish) and 心愿 (heartfelt wish), and works in blessings: 愿你平安 ("may you be safe").

components.note: 辶 (walk) — nearness is measured by how far one has to go
斤 (jīn) gives the sound — a near match for jìn

example.pinyin: Wǒ jiā lí xuéxiào hěn jìn.
example.english: My home is close to the school.
example.fact: 近 is the opposite of 远, with the key pattern A 离 B 很近 ("A is close to B"). 最近 means recently and 附近 means nearby. It also describes closeness of relationships, as in 亲近 (be close to).

components.note: 攵 (tap, action) — counting is done by tallying things one by one
娄 (lóu) gives a loose sound hint for the reading of 数

example.pinyin: Lái cānjiā de rénshù hěn duō.
example.english: The number of people who came is large.
example.fact: 数 has two common readings: shù means a number or amount (数字, 数学, 人数), and shǔ means to count (数一数, 数不清). The same character also appears in 数据 (data) and 数量 (quantity).

components.note: 日 (sun) is the base of the character, with a small stroke on top that is traditionally taken as a ray of light and linked to brightness

example.pinyin: Tā chuānzhe yí jiàn bái chènshān.
example.english: She is wearing a white shirt.
example.fact: 白 also means "in vain" (白跑一趟, a wasted trip) and "for free" (白吃白喝, to freeload). It builds 白天 (daytime) and 明白 (to understand), and white is the colour of mourning in traditional Chinese culture.

components.note: 火 (fire) — being cooked or burnt until falling apart
兰 (lán) gives the sound — a near match for làn

example.pinyin: Zhège píngguǒ làn le.
example.english: This apple has gone bad.
example.fact: 烂 covers both rotten food and soft-cooked food, a happy meaning in cooking: 炖烂 means stewed until tender. Colloquially it means lousy (烂人 for a bad person) and 烂尾楼 is an unfinished building abandoned halfway.

components.note: 身 (body) — hiding is done with your body
朵 (duǒ) gives the sound — an exact match

example.pinyin: Háizi duǒ zài mén hòumian.
example.english: The child is hiding behind the door.
example.fact: 躲 is to hide oneself or dodge, whereas 藏 (cáng) is to hide something. For hide-and-seek, people say 躲猫猫 or 捉迷藏. 躲避 is the formal "avoid", as in 躲避危险.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — moving in on someone, crowding them
畐 (fú) gives a loose sound hint for bī

example.pinyin: Bié bī wǒ, wǒ xūyào shíjiān.
example.english: Don't pressure me, I need time.
example.fact: 逼 means to force or press someone, often 逼 + person + verb: 逼我做. The idea of pressing close survives in 逼近 (to close in on) and 逼真 (lifelike, "pressing close to the real thing"). 被逼无奈 means "forced with no choice".

components.note: ⺈ stands for breath or an open mouth above the figure
人 (person) — the old picture is a person yawning with the mouth open

example.pinyin: Wǒ qiàn nǐ yí dùn fàn.
example.english: I owe you a meal.
example.fact: 欠 means to owe, not just money: 欠钱 (owe money), 欠你一个人情 (owe you a favour). It also means to lack, as in 欠缺. As a radical 欠 marks mouth actions, e.g. 吹, 歌, 欢.

components.note: 车 (vehicle) — a wheel belongs to a cart
仑 (lún) gives the sound — an exact match

example.pinyin: Zìxíngchē de lúnzi huài le.
example.english: The bicycle's wheel is broken.
example.fact: 轮 is a wheel and also the idea of turns: 轮到你了 ("it's your turn"), 轮流 (take turns). It counts rounds or cycles, as in 第一轮 (the first round) and is also the measure word for the sun or moon: 一轮明月.

components.note: Traditionally explained as a bird settling in its nest, borrowed for "west" because birds roost as the sun sets in the west

example.pinyin: Tàiyáng cóng xībiān luòxià.
example.english: The sun sets in the west.
example.fact: 西 is the direction west and also stands for "Western": 西餐 (Western food), 西方 (the West). Surprisingly, 东西 ("east-west") means "stuff, things", read dōngxi, and 西红柿 is the tomato, literally "western red persimmon".

components.note: 辶 (walk) — passing through along a road
甬 (yǒng) gives a loose sound hint for tōng

example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo lù bù tōng.
example.english: This road is blocked.
example.fact: 通 means to pass through or be unobstructed, in 通过 (pass through), 交通 (traffic) and 通知 (notify). As a result complement it means to get something through, as in 想通了 (finally understood). It is also a measure word for calls: 一通电话.

components.note: 疋 gives a loose sound hint for dàn
虫 (creature) — eggs are laid by small creatures

example.pinyin: Wǒ zǎofàn chī le yí gè jīdàn.
example.english: I had an egg for breakfast.
example.fact: 蛋 mostly appears in compounds: 鸡蛋 (chicken egg), 蛋糕 (cake, "egg cake") and 蛋白 (egg white/protein). It is also an insult word: 笨蛋 (idiot) and 坏蛋 (rascal).

components.note: 宀 (roof) — the traditional analysis sees something raised under a roof
子 (child) — a child under a roof: characters "give birth" to more characters

example.pinyin: Nǐ huì xiě zhège zì ma?
example.english: Can you write this character?
example.fact: 字 is a written Chinese character or syllable, such as 汉字, while a "word" in the linguistic sense is 词. A dictionary of characters is a 字典, and 字 was also the formal courtesy name of historical figures, e.g. 诸葛亮, 字孔明.

components.note: A simple picture of a pointed shape going into something, standing for entering

example.pinyin: Qǐng cóng rùkǒu jìnqu.
example.english: Please go in through the entrance.
example.fact: 入 forms 入口 / 出口 (entrance / exit) and verbs such as 加入 (join), 收入 (income) and 入学 (start school). It is also the name of the "entering tone" of Middle Chinese, which Mandarin no longer pronounces as a separate tone.

components.note: 圭 (stacked earth) — soil or mounds used to mark off land
寸 (hand) — a hand piling up earth to mark a boundary

example.pinyin: Wǒ zuótiān xiě le yì fēng xìn.
example.english: I wrote a letter yesterday.
example.fact: 封 is a measure word for letters and emails (一封信, 一封邮件). It also means to seal or close off: 封面 (cover), 封锁 (blockade), 封城 (lock down a city), and 封建 (feudal) comes from the old sense of granting land.

components.note: A picture of a fish — head, body and tail; the simplified form keeps the tail and fins in a reduced shape

example.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan chī yú.
example.english: I like eating fish.
example.fact: 鱼 counts with 条 (一条鱼). It is part of New Year symbolism because 鱼 (yú) sounds like 余 (surplus), so serving fish brings the wish 年年有余, "may there be surplus every year".

components.note: 身 here is a changed form of an old bow-and-arrow picture, not "body" in the modern sense
寸 (hand) — the hand that shoots

example.pinyin: Tā shèzhòng le mùbiāo.
example.english: He hit the target.
example.fact: 射 is to shoot an arrow or emit something: 发射 (launch), 射击 (shoot), 照射 (shine on) and 反射 (reflect). In football 射门 means to shoot at goal.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — a room is a space under a roof
至 (zhì) gives a loose sound hint for shì

example.pinyin: Wǒmen zài huìyìshì kāihuì.
example.english: We're holding a meeting in the meeting room.
example.fact: 室 is mostly a suffix: 教室 (classroom), 办公室 (office), 卧室 (bedroom), 浴室 (bathroom), 室友 (roommate). Apartment ads use it for layout: 两室一厅 means two bedrooms and one living room.

components.note: 酉 (wine jar) — drunkenness comes from alcohol
卒 (zú) gives a loose sound hint for zuì

example.pinyin: Tā hēzuì le, yìzhí zài chànggē.
example.english: He got drunk and kept singing.
example.fact: 醉 is mostly used as 喝醉 (get drunk) or 醉了 (be drunk). It extends to being enraptured: 陶醉 (be fascinated). 醉酒驾驶 is the legal term for drunk driving, and in slang 我醉了 can mean "I give up/I'm speechless".

components.note: 春 (chūn) gives the sound — a near match for chǔn
虫 (insect) — doubled, wriggling insects, which is the old sense of the word

example.pinyin: Wǒ zhēn chǔn, yòu wàng le dài yàoshi.
example.english: I'm so stupid, I forgot my keys again.
example.fact: 蠢 originally meant wriggling, like insects waking in spring, and that image still appears in 蠢蠢欲动 ("stirring and itching to act"). Today it means stupid, blunter than 笨 (bèn), which suggests clumsy or slow.

components.note: A tree (木) with an extra stroke above, traditionally read as a tree with fresh growth at its top

example.pinyin: Wǒ duì wèilái hěn yǒu xìnxīn.
example.english: I have a lot of confidence in the future.
example.fact: 未 is a formal "not yet" found in 未来 (future), 未成年 (minor), 未婚 (unmarried) and 未必 (not necessarily). In everyday speech it corresponds to 还没. It is also the eighth Earthly Branch of the zodiac cycle, linked to the sheep.

components.note: 彳 (step) — conduct, the way one walks through life
心 (heart) — virtue is a matter of the heart

example.pinyin: Tā shì ge pǐndé hěn hǎo de rén.
example.english: He is a person of very good character.
example.fact: 德 is virtue in 道德 (morality) and 品德 (moral character). It is also the short form of Germany, 德国, from 德意志 (Deutsch): 德语 is German, 中德 means China–Germany.

components.note: 甘 (sweet) sits on top; the old sense was a sour fruit tree, the word later borrowed for "a certain"
木 (tree) — the base of the character

example.hanzi: 某天，我在街上遇到了老同学。
example.pinyin: Mǒu tiān, wǒ zài jiē shang yùdào le lǎo tóngxué.
example.english: One day I ran into an old classmate on the street.
example.fact: 某 points to an unspecified person or thing: 某人, 某天, 某地. In news and legal texts it replaces a real surname to anonymise: 张某 means "a certain Zhang".

components.note: 自 (nose, the old meaning of this character) — smelling
犬 (dog) — a dog is the animal with the keenest nose

example.pinyin: Zhè shuāng wàzi hǎo chòu!
example.english: These socks stink!
example.fact: 臭 is smelly and also used for contempt: 臭美 (conceited), 臭脾气 (bad temper). 臭豆腐 (stinky tofu) is a beloved street food, and the character's original reading xiù ("smell") survives only in 乳臭未干 (still wet behind the ears).

components.note: 辶 (walk) — arriving is the end of a journey
大 (dà) gives the sound — they differ only in initial and tone

example.hanzi: 火车明天上午到达北京。
example.pinyin: Huǒchē míngtiān shàngwǔ dàodá Běijīng.
example.english: The train arrives in Beijing tomorrow morning.
example.fact: 达 is a bound verb, mostly in 到达 (arrive), 达到 (attain: 达到目标), 发达 (developed) and 表达 (express). In writing it also has the sense of reaching a total, as in 达三十人.

components.note: 钅 (metal) — bells are cast in metal
中 (zhōng) gives the sound — an exact match

example.pinyin: Qiáng shang de zhōng huài le.
example.english: The clock on the wall is broken.
example.fact: 钟 is a clock or a bell, and in time expressions it marks the hour: 三点钟 (three o'clock), 一个钟头 (an hour), 分钟 (minute). The simplified form merges the old, separate 鍾 and 鐘.

components.note: 疒 (sickness) — pain is a bodily ailment
冬 (dōng) gives a loose sound hint for téng

example.pinyin: Wǒ de tóu hěn téng.
example.english: My head hurts.
example.fact: 疼 is the everyday word for pain, more colloquial than 痛 (tòng), which is more formal or sharper. It also means to dote on: 妈妈很疼孩子 ("Mom adores her child"), 疼爱.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — notes and lots were once written on bamboo slips
佥 (qiān) gives the sound — an exact match

example.pinyin: Qǐng zài zhèlǐ qiānmíng.
example.english: Please sign your name here.
example.fact: 签 is to sign or put a signature to a document: 签名, 签字, 签证 (visa), 签约 (sign a contract). It is also a divination stick drawn at temples: 抽签 (draw lots). 牙签 is a toothpick.

meanings: measure word for small round things

components.note: 果 (guǒ) gives a loose sound hint for kē
页 (head) — the old sense was a small round head, the image of a little round object

example.pinyin: Tiānshang yǒu hěn duō kē xīngxing.
example.english: There are a lot of stars in the sky.
example.fact: 颗 counts small, round or grain-like things: 一颗星, 一颗糖, 一颗牙, 一颗心 (a heart). It is a bit more vivid or literary than 个, and the stricter 粒 is for tiny grains such as rice.

components.note: A picture of a piece of meat with the muscle lines marked inside

example.pinyin: Wǒ bù chī ròu, zhǐ chī cài.
example.english: I don't eat meat, only vegetables.
example.fact: Unqualified 肉 usually means pork in China (猪肉), with other meats named explicitly: 牛肉, 羊肉, 鸡肉. 肉 is also fruit flesh (果肉) and, as the radical ⺼, shows up in body parts such as 脚 and 肝.

components.note: Traditionally pictured as nuggets of metal buried in earth; the top part also hints at the sound 今 (jīn)

example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo xiàngliàn shì jīn zuò de.
example.english: This necklace is made of gold.
example.fact: 金 is gold and, more broadly, metal and money: 现金 (cash), 奖金 (bonus), 金钱. It is one of the Five Elements (金木水火土), and as a surname it is also how Korean Kim is written.

components.note: 龺 (the sun rising among grass) — the early-morning picture
月 (moon) — the moon still visible as day breaks

example.pinyin: Qǐng yìzhí cháo qián zǒu.
example.english: Please keep walking straight ahead.
example.fact: 朝 as cháo means "towards" and "dynasty": 朝向, 唐朝, 朝代. The older sense "morning" is read zhāo, as in 朝气蓬勃 (full of vitality) — a classic two-reading character.

components.note: 木 (wood) — early machines and looms were made of wood
几 (jī) gives the sound — an exact match

example.pinyin: Wǒ de shǒujī méi diàn le.
example.english: My phone is out of battery.
example.fact: 机 is a bound word for machines: 手机 (mobile phone), 飞机 (plane), 洗衣机 (washing machine), 机场 (airport). It also means opportunity: 机会, and 机器 is machine.

components.note: 土 (earth) — city walls were built of earth
成 (chéng) gives the sound — an exact match

example.hanzi: 我住在城里，不住在乡下。
example.pinyin: Wǒ zhù zài chéng lǐ, bú zhù zài xiāngxia.
example.english: I live in the city, not in the countryside.
example.fact: 城 originally meant the city wall, which was the defining feature of a city. 城市 is a city, 城里 means "in town" (versus 乡下), 长城 is the Great Wall, and 封城 means to lock a city down.

components.note: 户 (door) — a house or room has a door
方 (fāng) gives the sound — they differ only in tone

example.pinyin: Wǒmen gāng mǎi le yí tào fáng.
example.english: We just bought an apartment.
example.fact: 房 is a house or room, counted for apartments with 套 (一套房). It forms 房子 (house), 房间 (room), 厨房 (kitchen), 房租 (rent) and 房东 (landlord).

components.note: 禾 (grain) — the old sense was grain plants coming into ear
乃 (nǎi) is the lower part; its role in the sound is unclear

example.pinyin: Tā zhǎng de hěn qīngxiù.
example.english: She has delicate, refined looks.
example.fact: 秀 is elegant and refined (秀气, 清秀) and outstanding (优秀 excellent). It is also borrowed as the sound of English "show": 选秀 (talent show), 作秀 (to put on a show), 秀恩爱 (flaunt affection).

meanings: measure word for meals and scoldings

components.note: 页 (head) — the original idea is lowering the head, bowing
屯 (tún) gives the sound — a near match for dùn

example.pinyin: Wǒmen yì tiān chī sān dùn fàn.
example.english: We eat three meals a day.
example.fact: 顿 is the measure word for meals (一顿饭), and also for scoldings and beatings: 骂了一顿 (told off), 打了一顿 (beaten up). As a verb it means to pause (停顿), and 顿时 means "at once".

components.note: 亻 (person) — a person adapting things
更 (gēng, to change) — changing things to make them comfortable and easy

example.pinyin: Zhèlǐ zuò dìtiě hěn fāngbiàn.
example.english: Taking the subway here is very convenient.
example.fact: 便 is usually biàn (方便 convenient, 便利店 convenience store) — except in 便宜 (cheap), where it is read pián. In formal writing 便 also means "then, immediately", like 就.

components.note: 田 (field) — repeated field work wears you out
糸 (silk thread) — in the old reading, threads piling up as in accumulating

example.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān hěn lèi, xiǎng zǎodiǎn shuì.
example.english: I'm very tired today and want to sleep early.
example.fact: 累 has two readings: lèi (tired) and lěi (to accumulate, as in 积累 or 累计). As a verb, lèi can mean to tire someone out: 别累着, "don't wear yourself out". 累死了 is the everyday way to say "I'm exhausted".

components.note: Simplified form of 單; its pieces do not carry a clear meaning of their own

example.pinyin: Wǒ shì dānshēn, méiyǒu nǚpéngyou.
example.english: I'm single, I don't have a girlfriend.
example.fact: 单 is "single" (单身, 单独, 简单) and also a list or bill: 菜单 (menu), 账单 (bill), 名单 (name list). As a surname it is read Shàn, and in 单于 (the title of a ruler of the Xiongnu) it is read chán.

components.note: 木 (wood) — originally a kind of tree or wooden pattern
羊 (yáng) gives the sound — they differ only in tone

example.hanzi: 这件衣服的样子很好看。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu de yàngzi hěn hǎokàn.
example.english: This garment looks nice.
example.fact: 样 is a bound noun in everyday words: 样子 (appearance), 一样 (the same), 怎么样 (how about it?), 样品 (sample). The pattern A 和 B 一样 means "A is the same as B".

components.note: 冫 (ice) — coldness
令 (lìng) gives the sound — they share the same vowel

example.pinyin: Wàimiàn hěn lěng, duō chuān diǎn yīfu.
example.english: It's cold outside, wear more clothes.
example.fact: 冷 is strongly cold, while 凉 (liáng) is cool. It also describes people who are aloof (冷淡, 冷漠) or calm (冷静). 冷笑话 is a lame, deadpan joke, not a "cool" one.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — throwing is a hand action
殳 (shū) gives only a loose sound hint for tóu

example.pinyin: Tā bǎ qiú tóu jìn le lánzi lǐ.
example.english: He threw the ball into the basket.
example.fact: 投 means to throw or send in: 投票 (vote), 投篮 (shoot a basket), 投资 (invest), 投诉 (complain), 投稿 (submit an article) and 投信 (post a letter).

components.note: 耳 (ear) — the old sense of the word is hearing
门 (mén) gives the sound — they share the same final

example.pinyin: Wǒ wéndào yì gǔ xiāngwèi.
example.english: I smell a nice fragrance.
example.fact: In modern speech 闻 means "to smell" (闻到, 闻一闻), while "to hear" is 听. The hearing sense survives in 新闻 (news), 听闻 and 闻名 (famous). A common mistake is to use 闻 for hearing sounds.
